title: scikit-learn: Getting Started
description: Short official orientation to scikit-learn: fitting an estimator, transformers and pipelines, model evaluation and automatic parameter search.
why_useful: Introduces the fit/predict/transform interface that the whole library is built on, so every later scikit-learn page reads as a variation on one pattern rather than a new API.
learning_outcomes: Fit an estimator and make predictions
Compose preprocessing and a model into a pipeline
Run a basic parameter search

title: scikit-learn: Supervised learning
description: Reference chapter covering linear models, discriminant analysis, support vector machines, nearest neighbours, Gaussian processes, trees and ensembles.
quality_notes: A reference to consult per algorithm, not a linear read.
why_useful: Unusually good documentation that explains the statistical idea behind each estimator rather than only its parameters, which makes it a genuine learning resource and not just an API listing.
learning_outcomes: Choose an appropriate estimator family for a problem
Explain the assumptions behind common models
Map a textbook method onto its scikit-learn implementation

title: scikit-learn: Cross-validation, evaluating estimator performance
description: Official guide to train/test splitting, k-fold and stratified cross-validation, grouped splits, time-series splits and the pitfalls of each.
why_useful: This is the page that prevents the single most common beginner mistake: a validation split that leaks, producing a score that looks excellent and means nothing.
learning_outcomes: Choose a splitting strategy that matches your data's structure
Recognise leakage caused by preprocessing before splitting
Explain why grouped and time-series data need special handling

title: scikit-learn: Ensembles — gradient boosting, random forests, bagging, voting, stacking
description: Official coverage of ensemble methods, including bagging, random forests, gradient boosting, histogram-based boosting, voting and stacking.
why_useful: Gradient boosting remains the strongest default on tabular data, and often beats a neural network on it. Knowing this material prevents reaching for deep learning where it does not belong.
learning_outcomes: Explain the difference between bagging and boosting
Tune the parameters that actually matter for boosted trees
Decide when an ensemble is the right choice

title: scikit-learn: Preprocessing data
description: Official guide to scaling, normalisation, encoding categorical variables, discretisation, imputation and generating polynomial features.
why_useful: Feature preparation moves accuracy more than model choice on most tabular problems, and doing it inside a pipeline is what stops preprocessing from leaking across the validation split.
learning_outcomes: Scale and encode features appropriately for a chosen model
Fit preprocessing inside a pipeline to avoid leakage
Handle missing values as a modelling decision

title: scikit-learn: Clustering
description: Official comparison of clustering algorithms including k-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical and spectral clustering, with guidance on evaluation metrics.
why_useful: The side-by-side comparison makes clear that different algorithms find genuinely different notions of a cluster, which is the point people most often miss when results look plausible.
learning_outcomes: Pick a clustering algorithm suited to the data's shape
Evaluate clusters without ground-truth labels
Recognise when apparent structure is an artefact of the method

title: Machine Learning Crash Course
description: Structured course with video, text and interactive exercises covering linear and logistic regression, loss, gradient descent, generalisation, feature engineering and neural networks.
why_useful: One of the few free courses that is genuinely structured rather than a video list, with interactive exercises that force the concepts to stick before moving on.
learning_outcomes: Explain loss, gradient descent and generalisation
Diagnose overfitting and underfitting from curves
Build and evaluate a first end-to-end model

title: Interpretable Machine Learning
description: Free online book on making black-box models understandable, covering inherently interpretable models, partial dependence, permutation importance, LIME, Shapley values and SHAP.
author: Christoph Molnar
why_useful: Explains not just how each interpretation method works but where it misleads, which matters because these outputs are routinely presented to non-technical stakeholders as fact.
learning_outcomes: Choose an interpretation method suited to the model and question
Read a SHAP or permutation-importance plot critically
Explain the limits of post-hoc explanation

title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
description: Textbook covering regression, classification, resampling, regularisation, trees, support vector machines, unsupervised learning and more, with labs in R and Python.
author: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani
quality_notes: Check the site for which editions and labs are freely downloadable before assuming access.
why_useful: The standard bridge between statistics and machine learning: rigorous about why methods work, without requiring the measure theory that puts most textbooks out of reach.
learning_outcomes: Reason about the bias-variance trade-off concretely
Apply resampling methods to estimate error honestly
Understand regularisation as a statistical idea, not a knob

title: AI Principles
description: Google's published position on responsible AI development, including its stated principles and links to associated responsible-AI practices and tooling.
quality_notes: This is a company's own statement of intent, not an independent standard. Read it as one industry position among several, and note that such pages are revised over time.
why_useful: A concrete example of how a large organisation frames responsible AI commitments, useful as a starting point precisely because its interests are visible rather than hidden.
learning_outcomes: Describe common industry framings of responsible AI
Distinguish stated principles from enforceable practice
